items.body: Refs #5119 (remainder). Queue task 14074. Fixes the unresolved P2 from PR #8356's review (discussion r4532341753). ## Problem Slice 3 (PR #8356) persisted server-config provisioning into `directory.jsonl` beside the groups log. But a durable world loads its directory from `.id-worlds//directory.jsonl` (`world_store::open_world`), and nothing ever passed the provisioned accounts into that directory. Serving a durable world with `--server-config` therefore reported successful account provisioning at startup while the live world's directory view (`directory_view.rs`) treated the configured keys as anonymous. ## Fix - `Provisioned::apply_users` is extracted from `Provisioned::apply` (behaviour-preserving: `apply` now calls it first, then the group loop, with identical report semantics). This lets a directory that is not the provisioning home receive the same accounts without taking the group events, which belong to the groups log. - `cmd_serve`, after the config load and fail-fast provisioning, seeds the **default** world's directory (the world serve opens at startup) via the new `seed_world_directory` helper whenever world serving is on and the serve is not ephemeral. Seeding is the same idempotent account application, so a restart creates nothing and reports nothing new. - Ephemeral worlds hold no directory file, so there is nothing to seed; their state is in-memory and ends with the process, like the world itself. Worlds other than the default open lazily and are not seeded — the config's accounts are server-level identities, and the default world is the serving world the P2 scenario describes. ## Tests - New regression test `seed_world_directory_provisions_configured_accounts`: seeds a temp world directory from a two-user config, reopens it the way `world_store::open_world` does, asserts both accounts resolve, and asserts a second seed creates nothing. - Local verification (laptop, `--no-default-features --features world`, lib tests): `commands::serve::tests::` **47/47 pass** (incl. the slice-3 restart test and the pull-policy tests) and `server_config::` **57/57 pass**. Full default-feature suite is CI's verdict. ## Deliberately not in this PR The last #5119 remainder — wiring `ServerConfig::freshness()` into a seitan admission check that serve runs — has no consumer to wire into yet: `seitan::Invite::admit` takes the window as a parameter and has no production caller, and no serving path receives a seitan proof today. That remainder is being explicitly re-scoped on #5119 (it needs a serving admission path designed first), rather than being silently dropped or stubbed here. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.body: Slice 1 of #5119 (task 8839): the foundation that lets `id serve` consume `ServerConfig` at all — previously `ServerConfig::load` and `Provisioned::apply` had no production caller. ## What - **`--server-config `** on `id serve`, in the existing CLI style (cli.rs → main.rs → `ServeOptions` → `cmd_serve`). - When the flag is given, serve loads the config **before any startup work** via the new `start_server_config`: read/parse failures fail startup naming the `ServerConfig::parse` error and the path (the parser's startup-failing contract), and **`Provisioned::apply` runs from the loaded config**, with the report (users/groups/members created) on the startup status line. - The loaded config + provisioning stay in startup scope (`StartedServerConfig`) so slice 2 (pull gate from `config.pull_policy()`) and slice 3 (freshness into seitan admission) wire in from this one load. - **No flag = no file read and exactly today's behaviour.** On a binary built without the `world` feature (which owns `server_config`), the flag fails loudly, mirroring the existing `--web` guard. ## Tests (laptop, pkgs/id) - `cargo test --lib -- server_config` — 60 passed, including the 4 new serve tests: - `start_server_config_applies_provisioning` — a valid config loads; provisioning creates 2 users / 1 group / 1 member; a second apply over the same state creates nothing. - `start_server_config_fails_startup_on_a_malformed_file` — the parse error is named, with the path. - `start_server_config_fails_startup_on_a_missing_file`. - `serve_server_config_flag_defaults_to_none` — flag absent = `None`; `--server-config ops.toml` parses through. - `cargo test --lib -- commands::serve` — 37 passed. - `rustfmt --edition 2024` clean on the touched file. Out of scope per the slice definition: pull gate from config (slice 2), freshness wiring (slice 3), parse-surface changes. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(id): persist server-config provisioning into live serving state (#5119 slice 3)
items.body: Slice 3 of #5119 (queue task 14074): startup provisioning now lands in the live serving state instead of a throwaway in-memory value. ## What changed - `groups::log::GroupLog::record_preformed` — records an already-formed event keeping its ID and chain place; an event whose ID the log already holds is skipped, so seeding is a no-op after the first start. - `server_config::Provisioned::from_parts` — builds provisioning state from persisted parts (a journaled Directory + already-recorded group events); `apply` already skips what exists, so a restart creates nothing. - `serve::start_server_config_persisted` — serve now starts the config from persisted state: accounts into the journaled directory (`directory.jsonl` beside the groups log, the world-directory layout), preformed group events into the serve groups log itself — the same state live serving folds and replays. `cmd_serve` calls the persisted start; `--server-config` absent = unchanged behavior, and the slice-1 in-memory `start_server_config` remains for its existing tests/callers. ## Acceptance mapping (#5119) - Config-provisioned accounts and preformed group events are persisted/seeded into the state used by live serving: yes — directory journal + groups log. - A restart loads them without recreating them or reporting new creations: proven by `start_server_config_persisted_survives_a_restart` (second start reports `Report::default()`, accounts resolvable, events loaded back). - No-config behavior preserved: the persisted path only runs when `--server-config` is given. ## Tests - New: `groups::log` test_record_preformed_seeds_once_and_then_skips; `commands::serve` start_server_config_persisted_survives_a_restart. - Targeted runs on the laptop: see the task note on #5119 for the exact commands and results. ## Still remaining for #5119 (not this PR) - Wire config.freshness() into a real seitan admission check on the serve path. - Integration tests for member/non-member pulls + configured freshness through the live path. - #798 remainder / acceptance-brief handoff update. Refs #5119 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(id): serve builds its event-sync pull gate from [policy] (#5119 slice 2)
items.body: ## What Slice 2 of #5119: `id serve` now builds its live event-sync pull gate from the operator server config's `[policy] pull_policy`, on both accepted and dialled sessions. - `event_sync::gate(policy)` is the new constructor; `open_gate()` is now `gate(PullPolicy::Open)`. - `EventSyncProtocol::with_gate(...)` lets serve hand the configured gate to the accept side as well as the dial side. - With no `--server-config`, the policy is the code default (open) — behaviour is unchanged. - The local event store is not a world and has no membership source, so a configured `members` policy fails closed: every pull is refused, the startup log says so, and it never silently becomes open ([`NoWorlds`]). - Adds a test that a `Members` gate over a no-membership store sends and receives nothing. Thin slice: it lands the pull-policy half of remaining #5119. Still to do before #5119 can close (tracked on the issue and the queue task): 1. persist config-provisioned accounts / preformed group events into live serving state (restart idempotent), 2. wire `config.freshness()` into a real seitan admission check on the serve path, 3. integration tests for member/non-member pulls, provisioning/restart, no-world handling, configured freshness, 4. verify/update the #798 remainder + acceptance-brief handoff line. Closes nothing on its own; part of #5119. ## Tests - `cargo check -p id --all-targets` — pass - `cargo test -p id event_sync` — running locally (result noted in review) Opened by the OpenChamber scheduled repo-health lane (queue task 14074, lane `02cafe76-eafd-4d0b-aaa6-2b7a737d68dc`). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(id): wire serve loaded budgets into WorldProtocol (#2247)
items.body:
## Summary
- Wire the loaded server config's #2247 budget policy into the production `WorldProtocol` that `id serve` registers: `cmd_serve` now builds the protocol through a new `world_protocol_for` helper, which passes `started.config.budgets().clone()` to `WorldProtocol::with_budgets` when `--server-config` was given, and keeps `with_local_node` (coded defaults) when it was not.
- Before this, the `[budgets]` table was parsed and held at startup scope (`_started_server_config`) but never reached the protocol, so configured per-counterparty caps were inert in production. The binding is renamed to `started_server_config` now that it has a live consumer.

## Tests — status (2026-11-10, task 9172, lane code-m)
- New tests: `serve_world_protocol_enforces_configured_budgets` (a config with `per_peer_bytes_per_hour` plus a `[[budgets.counterparty]]` row produces a protocol whose evaluator carries exactly that policy; the counterparty row replaces the peer's limits via `limits_for_peer`; a 600-byte charge against the 500-byte window is refused `RefusalReason::BudgetExhausted` — frame dropped, peer not disconnected) and `serve_world_protocol_defaults_budgets_without_config` (no config → `BudgetPolicy::default()`).
- **The new tests have not run yet**: the `id` lib test target does not compile on current main for an unrelated, pre-existing reason — `pkgs/id/src/world_store.rs` tests use `JOURNAL_VERSION_EXECUTION_PROFILE` unqualified (E0599, sole error in the build; serve.rs itself compiles with no errors). That break is issue #7081, already owned by task 14503. When it lands: `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml --lib serve_world_protocol` and `--lib budget`, then merge this PR.

Scope per task 9172: no parser or BudgetPolicy semantics changed; #5119 pull-gate/freshness untouched.

Refs #2247 (the config/parser surface landed earlier; this is the serve wiring remainder).

items.title: feat(id): seitan admission path for id serve (#8487)
items.body: Implements #8487 (task 14862, lane code-p), per the design recorded on the issue by task 14857 (comment 6786323656). On merge: check off the #798 brief line-76 item and close #5119 with this evidence (its last open item) — handled by the task's completion pass, not this PR body alone. ## What lands **Serve web surface (`pkgs/id/src/web/seitan.rs`, new)** — `SeitanState`: the invite registry (`HashMap`), the server's `Directory`, and the resolved freshness window behind one mutex; clones share the one registry. - `POST /api/seitan/invite` — registration, gated by the same admin-secret check as `POST /api/world/invite` (hub lease for the named world + `admin_ok` on the `x-world-admin-token` header; no hub → 404, busy → 503, bad/absent secret → 401). Body `{token, world, expires_ms}`; the server builds `Invite::create(token, now, expires_ms)` and stores it; the response carries only the invite ID. The token is never stored (`Invite` keeps ID + public key + expiry by construction) and never logged. - `POST /api/seitan/admit` — unauthenticated; the signed proof is the credential. Body `{message, signature}`, both hex. Handler order per the design: unparseable proof → 400 `malformed`; no registry entry → 404 `unknown_invite` (nothing consumed); `uid` naming no directory account → 403 `unknown_account`, checked from the parsed fields **before** `admit`, so the invite is not consumed; `Invite::admit` refusal → 403 with the `Reject` reason (`revoked`/`expired`/`used`/`stale`/`from_future`/`bad_key`/`bad_signature`); success appends `AccountVerified` via `Directory::verify_account(Actor::Server, …)` **before** the 200 `{uid, eldest_seqno, world}` — if the append fails after a successful admit, a loud 500 and the invite stays consumed (single-use safety over retry convenience). - The world an admission joins is the world bound at registration, never taken from the proof. - Registry is v1 in-memory: a restart drops unredeemed invites, which then refuse as unknown — acceptable for short-lived invites; persistence is a named follow-up only if operations need it. **Window (`pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs`)** — `serve_freshness_window(started)` mirrors `serve_pull_policy`: `started.config.freshness().window()` when a server config is loaded, `seitan::DEFAULT_WINDOW` (5 min) when none is. In `cmd_serve`, the `SeitanState` is built with that window and a `Directory` opened on the server-config directory journal beside the groups log (after provisioning persisted into it, so provisioned accounts are visible to the admit account check) and threaded through `web::web_routers` → `finish_router` → `AppState.seitan` (the same pattern as `groups_log`). Other router constructors keep the default state. ## Tests - Five integration tests in the `web/routes.rs` test idiom (tower oneshot over `create_router`), plus the admin-gate test: (a) happy path under a non-default configured window — a proof signed 8 min before invite creation (outside the 5-min default, inside the configured 10-min) admits and `AccountVerified` lands in the directory; (b) a proof signed 5 min before creation under a 1-min configured window refuses `stale` through the live path; (c) no-config default state admits a fresh proof under the default window; (d) unknown invite → 404 `unknown_invite`; (e) unknown account → 403 `unknown_account`, then the same proof succeeds after the account is keyed in (invite not consumed); (f) invite registration without/with a wrong admin secret → 401. - `serve_freshness_window` unit tests mirroring the `serve_pull_policy` pair (no-config default; configured 60 s window read from `[policy] freshness_window_seconds`). - Existing seitan and serve suites stay green (targeted runs recorded on task 14862). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): preserve unused link reference definitions
items.body: ## Summary ```text definition recovery collect reference labels used by links and images include references synthesized while recovering orphan footnotes append only unused definitions using the existing HTML-block carrier ``` Saving keeps definitions-only documents and unused definitions without adding an editor schema node. The existing `code_block`/`htmlBlock` representation carries the preserved source through the editor. Fixes #1004 ## Evidence - **Before:** current main runs only `preserve_unreferenced_footnote_definitions`; #1004's triage confirms unused definitions are dropped and definitions-only files save empty. - **After:** `cd pkgs/id && cargo test -p id --features web web::markdown` — 237 passed, 0 failed. - `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 src/web/markdown.rs` — pass. - Added coverage for body-plus-unused definitions, definitions-only input, full/collapsed/shortcut/image used references, literal contexts, and save fixpoints. - `cargo fmt --check` still reports unrelated existing formatting diffs elsewhere in the workspace; the changed file passes directly. ## Merge Danger **Door:** Two-way; revert the commit to restore the previous codec behavior. **Blast Radius:** Narrow — id web Markdown load/save only. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Preserved unused Markdown link-reference definitions when parsing, while keeping references used by links and images inline. * Improved preservation across literal content, nested containers, and line breaks. * Ensured recovered footnotes account for references they use. * Added coverage for definitions-only documents and save/reopen consistency.
